title: improve(ui): load the chat Review panel on demand instead of at boot
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat boot downloads the whole Review side panel (file, attachment, PDF/HTML preview and diff views) before anyone opens it. `chat-sidebar.ts` imported `chat-detail-panel.ts` for its side effect, so the panel and its subtree sat in the measured boot groups. The same subtree then also reached New Session's boot set, even though New Session already loads the panel lazily. When this PR was opened, that eager subtree pushed the largest boot chunk to 217.1 KiB, over the 215 KiB budget. `main` has since brought the budget back under separately (198a4bed8b03 narrowed the shared partition size), so this PR is now about boot bytes, not the budget.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session boot no longer download the Review panel. It loads on first open, behind the panel's existing review loading skeleton, the same way the terminal, browser, desktop and other side panels already load. Tool output in the side panel still renders immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar already owns lazy panel elements (`LAZY_SIDEBAR_ELEMENTS` / `ensureLazySidebarElement` in `chat-pane-sidebar-layout.ts`), with loading, error and stale-chunk recovery. The Review panel was the one element still registered eagerly. This change:

- drops the side-effect import from `chat-sidebar.ts`, which is now a type and helper barrel;
- makes `renderChatDetailSlot` load `openclaw-chat-detail-panel` through `ensureLazySidebarElement` under a non-slot `detail-panel` key, the same pattern `region` uses. Only the panel branch waits; tool output, the slot's loading state and the unavailable callout stay synchronous;
- regenerates `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` with `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` (current generator from #162382);
- updates tests that imported `chat-sidebar.ts` only to define the panel so they import `chat-detail-panel.ts` directly.

No budget, `maxSize`, minifier or naming changes.

Compared with a fresh regeneration of `main` (`a272cf0cd56e`), the PR's manifest has identical route entries. It drops 25 modules from `shared`: the panel subtree leaves boot entirely, and 12 modules New Session only reached through the eager panel (file view, diff render, draft recovery and others) move to the `chat` group. The manifest's remaining differences from `main`'s committed file are `main`'s own drift since its last regeneration; regenerating unmodified `main` produces the same drift (+95 shared modules).

## Evidence

Same machine and toolchain, `pnpm ui:build` + `pnpm ui:check-performance`, merged head vs `main` @ `a272cf0cd56e`:

| Metric | `main` (committed manifest) | `main` + fresh manifest regen | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/chat` boot JS | 1459.6 KiB, 32 req | 1482.5 KiB, 33 req | **1467.8 KiB, 32 req** |
| `/new` boot JS | 1170.1 KiB, 27 req | 1242.2 KiB, 28 req | **1217.1 KiB, 27 req** |
| Largest ordinary JS | 179.2 KiB (`ghostty-web`) | 197.9 KiB (`control-ui-boot-shared`) | **194.5 KiB** (`control-ui-boot-shared`) |
| Startup JS | 364.1 KiB, 8 req | 363.7 KiB, 8 req | 363.7 KiB, 8 req |

The middle column is the like-for-like baseline. Against it, the PR saves 14.7 KiB gzip and one request on `/chat` and 25.1 KiB gzip and one request on `/new`. All three pass `ui:check-performance`.

Verification:

- On the merged head: `pnpm ui:check-performance` passed; `pnpm --dir ui test` on chunking, sidebar layout and its lazy-failure test, embedded panels, chat sidebar, and new-session page passed (103 tests); `tsgo:ui` and the `tsgo:test:ui` shards passed; `oxfmt --check` clean.
- Before the merge, a Blacksmith Testbox run (`tbx_01m3tk3nftzfy89exvckqtkb81`) passed with limits enforced: `ui:build`, `ui:check-performance`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, 418 tests across the 20 affected unit and browser files, and 22 mocked-browser e2e cases across the four flows that open the Review panel on `/chat` (`chat-text-attachment`, `chat-file-links`, `chat-side-panel-clearance`, `chat-html-preview`). An earlier design that made the whole Review slot wait (including tool output) failed those e2e flows; the shipped design gates only the panel element.
- Test cost: no new tests. Edited tests only swap a side-effect import for the panel module they exercise or pass a `requestUpdate` callback.

No visual change: the first open of the Review panel shows the panel's existing loading skeleton until the module arrives.

<details>
<summary>Original budget investigation (main @ 12220221ffeb, before 198a4bed8b03)</summary>

Rolldown splits each boot group into `maxSize` partitions by sorting modules by path and bisecting at directory boundaries. The oversized partition was every shared-boot module under `ui/src/pages/chat/components/` (1.34 MB source), so its gzip size tracked that one directory run. Moving code between boot groups just refills another partition: an experiment that moved 2.1 MB of chat-only code out of `shared` raised the largest chunk to 239 KiB.

Sampled main builds, same toolchain: the largest shared chunk was 210.3 KiB on 09-23, crept to 215.0 KiB by 09-27, then the Tasks/TaskFlow removal (#159179) reset it to 204.7 KiB. It regrew to 211.3 KiB by 09-29 and jumped to 217.1 KiB overnight into 09-30. Per-module attribution of that last +5.9 KB jump: emoji reactions (#161053) +2.45 KB, CI popup automation controls (#161492) +2.41 KB, the "Replying to" line (#150549) about +1.7 KB, inter-session receipts (#161656) about +0.8 KB (that PR also moved transcript layout modules into a stable chunk, offsetting about 3.7 KB). Earlier in the window, camera capture (#160253) and the draft recovery dialogs (#159414, #158213) landed in the same directory run.

On that base this PR measured 217.1 → 203.4 KiB for the largest chunk, while a regeneration-only control stayed at 217.1 KiB.

</details>
